issues.description: The problem statement UML and solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch between the template and the specification/solution can confuse students about which method to call when adding a new StockIngredient and may cause compilation errors if they follow the UML or solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem specification: rename the template's addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or provide an alias addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem). Update the template code comments and any references so students see the same method name as in the UML and solution.

issues.description: The Stock class method for adding a StockIngredient is named addItem(StockIngredient) in the template repository but is documented as addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the problem statement UML and implemented as addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the solution. This inconsistent identifier for the same concept (adding an ingredient object into the stock inventory) can confuse students when mapping the UML and problem requirements to the provided template code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to match the UML/problem statement and the solution, or provide an addToStockIngredients wrapper that delegates to addItem so the template, problem description, and solution use the same identifier for the same operation.
